The choice to participate in a system of laws precedes acceptance of the laws of that system. Secession is a question of the people's natural right to choose their governance, and therefore supercedes any written law.

The Spanish Constitution is fairly recent, as it only dates back to 1978. From 1975 to 1978, all the territories who wanted to secede from Spain might have had their chance, as the legal framework which turned the country into what it is now didn't exist.

The choice to participate in this system of laws was clear in the 1978 Constitutional referendum, which had a proportion of 90~92% of 'Yes' votes in all four Catalan provinces. Subsequently the Constitution was approved, and as per this new legal framework, Spain was divided in 17 regions, called "Autonomous Communities". Catalonia is therefore almost fully autonomous. They have their own railways administration, their own correctional system, their own educational system, healthcare system, police corps, firefighter corps, etc., which is way more than other regions in Spain. 1. If time travel is possible, it is inevitable.

  2. If time travel is inevitable, it has already occurred.

  3. If time travel has already occurred, we are living in a post time travel society.

Most of the philosophy I've looked up regarding time travel is much conjecture as to whether or not it is possible. The possibility of time travel is a very long, and very complicated subject and ultimately not as interesting as the consequences of its future implementation. This post shall make the assumption that time travel is possible and go over some of the implications.

Time Travel - The ability to transmit information or action backward in time. To a lesser extent, the ability to abridge subjective time for a subject such that they arrive at a future date at a rate better than a second per second.

If you have the ability to send information backward in time, and this ability is easily done without much trouble, things get out of hand very quickly. Assuming a positive outcome scenario, effectively you could have the answer to any question you could ask as soon as you ask it. Messages sent to you from the future would be sent back with 20/20 hindsight as to what would work for any given action. For example, say you ask a time-travel capable walkie talkie how to solve world hunger. The message that you get would allow you to do just that.

You'll notice I'm assuming a positive outcome here. If we assume a negative outcome, the outcome results in a bad course of action, the effects would be deleterious to the future, and the future could not have life within it to send back the message. What I'm describing is a feedback loop where every positive effect for the future is amplified to its best possible outcome for those in the future and any negative outcome for the future is "tuned-out" by the fact that negative outcomes won't be sent back; it would be either the time travel effect functions or it would appear not to function as there is nobody on the "receiving end" so to speak.

Now, once you invent a device capable of reverse-flow information transfer, you have just given the entire future the 2.0 version, the 3.0 version, all the way up to the infinite version. So we can assume that the future, which presumably has no fixed end date, has the best mode of time travel at its disposal. In some ways, this is like handing the conquistadors the keys to the kingdom. In other ways, assuming the future is in some way dependent upon you for their continued survival, you have them by the balls. (Possibly even your balls.)

From the point time travel is invented onward, it is probably safe to say that time travel is quite easy. Prior to that point, however, things become increasingly difficult as any event sent back in time before the invention of time travel must lead to the inevitable invention of time travel. Here I see two possibilities.

  1. Alternate Universe Creation Time Travel - This method changes "the past" in some way using some method such that the events that occur after the change lead to an entirely new universe.

  2. Fixed Universe Time Travel - You can make changes to things so long as these changes are things that have already happened.

Of these two, I suspect 1 is less likely or less possible and 2 is more likely and perhaps the only possibility. First, method 1 would require enough energy exerted at a future date to create a new universe. Presumably this requires a fantastic amount of energy and could conceivably destroy those in the universe attempting the alteration. This would seem to be a bad method. Method 2, on the other hand, requires very little excess energy. In fact, it may even be facilitated by the fact that the change has already been made. This would seem on the surface to be a very useless type of time travel, but I could see a few instances in which it would be useful. For example, you could change something in the past such that it is unobserved until such time as it is needed after the alteration is made. So hide a secret robot army in the core of the moon or perpetually behind Jupiter relative to us and all observers, only to deploy after the date their message is sent back. This would eliminate the need to have your message include time-travel within itself, which is probably computationally difficult.

However, considering the last people to have time travel presumably also have the best method of time travel, they would also have an unlimited amount of time with which to craft their message. They would effectively be able to do anything they wish with it; cure death, save people from the past, unlimited food or eliminated need for food, effectively infinite wisdom, what have you. Considering their power, presumably these people could choose which parties would be the ones to invent time travel in the first place, among other things.

Of course, considering most tools ever used are inevitably used in war, it is very likely that there would be a time war. Now, what would be the point of the time war? Wouldn't the victor be known in advance? Likely so. This is probably a dense enough topic for its own post.

As you can see, this is a very difficult subject to tackle and I've started in the middle. I also haven't yet gone to look for evidence of it already happening. This is a work in progress. For now, I'm going to leave this here and possibly polish it up as need be. I hope you have fun with this little thought experiment.

  • Positive Paradox and Negative Paradox

  • Morality and Time Travel

  • How Possible is Time Travel?

  • Time travel as a modern parable for improved understanding of God
